purpose: Teach: チャイナ/ウエスト/浦和/三島/ジェフ/クラーク/コロンビア/セントラル

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがチャイナドレスの妻を見て喜ばれた
lines.en: You know, when your father was young, he saw a woman in a cheongsam and was so pleased.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Slow, measured pace. Warm affection in the voice, like touching something fragile from decades ago. Slight upward lift at the end, inviting her to remember with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、晩年もウエストサイズに気をつけられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and didn't you watch your waistline all through your later years too, my dear?
lines.style: Playful teasing underneath genuine tenderness. Quick, knowing smile in the voice. Light rhythm that bounces slightly, affectionate rather than sharp. Warm eye-contact level, not looking away.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが浦和の親戚を訪ねられた
lines.en: When your father was young, he'd visit our cousins out in Urawa.
lines.style: Soft, reflective. Settling into another memory. Same gentle distance as before. The voice traces the memory lightly, not forcing it. Breathing is easy, unhurried.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、三島由紀夫の文学を語って下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he'd talk to us about Mishima's writings, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm acknowledgment of shared history. Slight knowing smile. Voice has the texture of 'we both remember this.' Gentle affirmation rather than question, even though the words ask. Breath is soft and present.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがジェフ・ベックのギターを聴かれた
lines.en: In those days, your father loved listening to Jeff Beck's guitar.
lines.style: Drifting further into the past. Voice becomes quieter, more internal. Pace slows even more. There's a small wonder in it — remembering something specific and alive. Trailing slightly, as if he can almost hear it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、クラーク博士の「少年よ大志を抱け」が好きだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He had such a love for William Clark's words — 'Boys, be ambitious.' You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Tender recognition of shared memory. Soft emphasis on the phrase itself, like it still matters. Voice has warmth and a touch of ceremony. Breath is calm, the question genuine but rhetorical — she'll know.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがコロンビアコーヒーを愛飲された
lines.en: Your father had a real passion for Colombian coffee in those days.
lines.style: Another gentle return to memory. Voice is intimate, not performing. Pace is unhurried, almost meditative. Slight smile in the delivery, remembering something small and human. Open, not trailing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ニューヨークのセントラルパークの写真集をお持ちだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you kept that lovely photograph collection of Central Park in New York, didn't you, love?
lines.style: Final memory, delivered with deep affection and gentle closure. Voice has warmth and a touch of wonder. Soft, close delivery — like speaking to her across a small space. Slight fade at the end, intimate and present.
